chapters.title: The Workshop
chapters.subtitle: 2 a.m., a garage and a hand-painted sign: PHONE REPAIR

steps.hint: Walk to the door and press E. Too dark? F turns on the flashlight.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: The door sticks. Lift the handle and push. The garage respects confidence.

steps.hint: The switch is on the wall by the door. Look at it and press E.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Let there be light! A repair shop in the dark is just a scary garage.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Bench, counter, bell. The bell is the most important tool here. Trust me.

steps.objective: Take the device from the counter
steps.hint: Press E at the counter to accept the order, then carry the device to the bench.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Ding-ding! Your first customer. Smile, they can smell fear. And solder.

steps.hint: Put it on the repair bench and press E: open it up, find the fault, fix it, close it.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Lamp on, magnifier down. Screws go in the cup, not in your pocket.

steps.objective: Return it at the counter and get paid
steps.hint: Carry it back and press E at the counter. A neater repair pays more.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Fixed? Now the best part: a happy face and real money.

steps.hint: Playing together? One of you takes orders, another repairs. Faster than heroics.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Word travels fast on this street. Here comes another one.

chapters.title: Spare Parts
chapters.subtitle: You can't fix a screen with good intentions

steps.objective: Take the new order to the bench
steps.hint: Press E at the counter, then take a close look at the device on the bench.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Ooh, that one's crunchy. I think it needs a new part, not just a screwdriver.

steps.objective: Call the supplier on the wall phone
steps.hint: Press E on the phone on the wall. It opens Purchasing.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: No screens left? You can't fix glass with good intentions.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Call Zip. Zip answers at any hour. I'm not sure Zip sleeps at all.

steps.hint: Find the screens in the list and buy a few. A handful is plenty for now.

lines.speaker: zip
lines.text: Zip Parts, Zip speaking! Screens, batteries, ports. What broke, friend?

lines.speaker: zip
lines.text: Delivered before your tea gets cold. Unless it's iced tea. Then it's a race.

steps.objective: Fit the new part at the bench
steps.hint: Back to the bench: the new part goes in during the repair.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Old glass out, new glass in. Gently. It's thinner than my patience.

steps.objective: Return the device and get paid
steps.hint: The price covers the part, so you still make a profit. Good business!

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Your customer is still waiting. Bravely. Let's not test that bravery.

chapters.title: The Same Fault
chapters.subtitle: Every phone breaks in the same place. Interesting…

steps.hint: Two customers, two broken ports. Out of ports? Buy more in Purchasing.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Two customers at once, and both with broken charging ports. Hmm.

steps.hint: Listen to Aunt Mira. Something is going on with these phones.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Same port, same wobble, same model. Third one this week.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Phones are designed by people who never drop phones. You drop them daily. That's an advantage.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: You fix them one by one. What if you built one that doesn't break?

steps.objective: Start your first research at the whiteboard
steps.hint: Press E at the whiteboard and pick a technology. The first one is free.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Fixing one phone is a repair. Fixing all of them is called research.

steps.hint: A quick mini-game pushes the research forward. Optional, but fun.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Markers out! Bad ideas first: they're blocking the door for the good ones.

chapters.title: Our Own Phone
chapters.subtitle: What if we built one that doesn't break?

steps.objective: Meet the visitor at the door
Design your first phone on the PC
steps.hint: PC → Design Studio. The defaults work; just fix what your customers hated.

lines.speaker: felix
lines.text: Remember the wobbly ports and the batteries that die by noon? Start there.

steps.hint: On the last step press "Begin development". Your prototype is on its way.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: A name, a price and one button. The scariest button in this garage.

steps.hint: The clock runs now: speed it up, or help with a bug hunt at the PC.

lines.speaker: felix
lines.text: Development is like soup. Don't lift the lid every five minutes.

steps.hint: Sit on the PC chair for a quick bug hunt. Optional.

lines.speaker: felix
lines.text: Found a bug? Good. Better you than the critics.

chapters.title: First Batch
chapters.subtitle: Handmade, one tiny screw at a time

steps.objective: Start a batch at the workbench
steps.hint: Press E at the workbench, pick your phone and a quantity. Materials come from Purchasing.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Hand assembly! Like the old days, only with fewer burns. Hopefully.

steps.hint: Finished phones are packed into crates next to the workbench.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Every phone in that crate was made by your hands. Strange feeling, right?

steps.objective: Carry a crate to the van and ship it
steps.hint: Grab the crate and put it in the van. Careful handling gives +5% units.

lines.speaker: felix
lines.text: Gently! That box is our future. And my investment. Mostly my investment.

steps.hint: Spot the faulty phones for a few extra units. Optional.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Check every phone as if a customer will drop it. Because they will.

chapters.title: Launch Night
chapters.subtitle: Spotlights, critics and a brand-new sign

steps.hint: Press E at the stage when you're ready. The critics are already seated.

lines.speaker: critic
lines.text: Good evening, I'm Vera Benchmark. Three thousand phones reviewed. Every single one dropped.

lines.speaker: critic
lines.text: A team from a garage? Let's see if it survives my pocket. And my stairs.

steps.hint: Whatever the score, you shipped a real phone. Most people only talk about it.

lines.speaker: critic
lines.text: Off the record: I dropped it twice on the way here. Respect.

steps.objective: Hang up the new company sign
steps.hint: Watch the old sign come down.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: One more thing, my dears. That old sign doesn't fit you anymore.

customers.name: Grandma Rosa
customers.fault: Calls her ex-husband by itself. They split up in 1979

lines.arrive: Good evening, dears! My grandson says this is a phone. I mostly use it to crack walnuts.
lines.story: It keeps calling my ex-husband all by itself. We split up in 1979! He's very confused.
lines.wait: Take your time. I brought pies. Well, I brought pies for me.
lines.happy: Wonderful! Here's {money}. And a pie. Don't tell my grandson about the walnuts.
lines.angry: In my day repairs were quicker. And walnuts were softer.

customers.name: Max the Student
customers.fault: Side button stuck after a thousand snoozed alarms

lines.arrive: Hi… sorry, I slept two hours. Can phones be fixed on a student budget?
lines.story: I snoozed my alarm so many times the button just gave up. Now it's stuck forever.
lines.wait: I'll just close my eyes for a second. Wake me when it's ready. Or never.
lines.happy: You're heroes! Here's {money}. That was my whole noodle budget for the week.
lines.angry: I could have slept through this whole repair. I almost did.

customers.name: Dina the Courier
customers.fault: Dropped it carrying a cake up nine floors. The cake survived

lines.arrive: Quick, quick! I've got four minutes and eleven parcels.
lines.story: I carried a cake up nine floors and dropped my phone on the last step. The cake survived!
lines.wait: My break is four minutes. Three now. Two and a half…
lines.happy: Like new! Here's {money}. Five stars, and I'm giving them fast!
lines.angry: Too slow! I could have delivered forty pizzas by now.

customers.name: Mr. Pell the Teacher
customers.device: Phone in a very sensible case
customers.fault: Charging port packed with thirty years of chalk dust

lines.arrive: Good evening. No rush, please. Patience is the first thing I teach. Spelling is the second.
lines.story: The charging port is full of chalk dust. Thirty years at the blackboard. The chalk finally won.
lines.wait: While we wait: who can name three parts of a phone? Hands up, please.
lines.happy: Excellent work. Here's {money}. An A-plus, and I almost never give those.
lines.angry: I will grade this repair later. Expect a C minus.

customers.name: Kit the Gamer
customers.fault: "Didn't throw it, it flew." The port left with the cable

lines.arrive: Hey. Okay, first of all: I didn't throw it. It flew.
lines.story: The cable stayed in the wall and the charging port kind of… went with it. Lag did this.
lines.wait: Is there Wi-Fi here? Asking for my other phone.
lines.happy: GG! It charges! Here's {money}. That's a week of lunch money, you know.
lines.angry: Laaag. Even my grandma's router is faster.

customers.name: Lou the Barista
customers.fault: Dipped it in the milk jug while making latte art

lines.arrive: Hi-hi! I brought you coffee. Well, I brought me coffee, but you can smell it.
lines.story: I was drawing a heart on a latte and dipped my wrist right into the milk. Now it's a milkshake watch.
lines.wait: This is longer than a triple espresso. But shorter than decaf. I'm fine.
lines.happy: You're the best! Here's {money}. Free cappuccinos for you all week.
lines.angry: My coffee went cold. My heart did too. A little.

customers.name: Sam the Taxi Driver
customers.fault: Navigation on 16 hours a day. The battery has seen the whole city

lines.arrive: Evening, chief! Sam the taxi. I know every street in this city and every pothole by name.
lines.story: Navigation runs sixteen hours a day. This battery has seen more of the city than I have.
lines.wait: I once drove a famous singer down this street. Can't say who. Starts with a letter.
lines.happy: Top service! Here's {money}. Need a ride anywhere? Half price, for you.
lines.angry: The meter's running, friends! Well, it would be, in my taxi.

customers.name: Jo the Drummer
customers.fault: A drumstick flew off during a solo. Right into the screen

lines.arrive: Yo! Jo, drummer. Don't worry, I left my drums at home. Mostly.
lines.story: Epic drum solo, the stick slipped and flew straight into my laptop screen. Best solo of my life, though.
lines.wait: Ba-dum-tss. Sorry, I drum on everything when I wait.
lines.happy: Sounds perfect! Here's {money}. You're all on the guest list now.
lines.angry: This repair is slower than our bass player. And that's saying something.

customers.name: Chef Arno
customers.device: Recipe tablet in a flour-dusted case
customers.fault: The charging port is packed with flour

lines.arrive: Good evening, my friends! Chef Arno. I trust you with this like I trust my best knife.
lines.story: My tablet helped me make dumplings. Now the charging port is packed with flour.
lines.wait: Patience is like dough, my friends. Leave it alone and it rises.
lines.happy: Chef's kiss! Here's {money}. Come eat at my place. Tablets stay away from the dough.
lines.angry: Overcooked! Like this repair. Far too long, my friends.

customers.name: Mia the Blogger
customers.fault: Selfie stick vs. ceiling fan. The fan won

lines.arrive: Hiii, chat! We're at a real repair shop! Say hi to my followers!
lines.story: My selfie stick met a ceiling fan. The fan won. Can I film you fixing it?
lines.wait: Waiting content! So authentic. Okay, I'm bored.
lines.happy: Obsessed! Here's {money}. I'm tagging you in everything.

cracked_screen.name: Cracked screen
cracked_screen.story: Long story. Goat yoga. A goat stepped on it. The goat is fine.

dead_battery.name: Dead battery
dead_battery.story: It counted forty thousand steps and died. I think it's just tired.

broken_port.name: Broken charging port
broken_port.story: A toddler at a party tried to charge it with a banana. The banana is fine.

water_damage.name: Water damage
water_damage.story: The box said waterproof. The lake disagreed.

software_glitch.name: Software glitch
software_glitch.story: Since Tuesday it only speaks German. I don't. It seems happy, though.

stuck_button.name: Stuck button
stuck_button.story: My cat slept on it all week. The button gave up before the cat did.

captions.speaker: radio
captions.text: Night Shift FM, two a.m. Somewhere out there, a phone just slipped into a bathtub.

captions.speaker: radio
captions.text: And somewhere, a few friends are opening a repair shop in a garage. Good luck, night owls.

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: A quiet street. A rented garage. A hand-painted sign: PHONE REPAIR.

captions.speaker: mira
captions.text: The garage is yours, my dears. Rent is cheap: fix my kettle once a month.

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: Tonight the shop opens. Tomorrow? Nobody knows yet.

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: A very quiet car stops outside. Electric, shiny and clearly expensive.

captions.speaker: felix
captions.text: Evening! I'm Felix, Mira's brother. She says you fix phones at 2 a.m. and talk to them kindly.

captions.speaker: felix
captions.text: I made my fortune on robot vacuums. They kept getting stuck under sofas, so I fixed that.

captions.speaker: felix
captions.text: I don't invest in companies. I invest in people who open things up just to see why they broke.

captions.speaker: felix
captions.text: Here's {money}. Build a phone I can't break. I'll try very, very hard.

captions.speaker: mira
captions.text: He broke three of my kettles. Believe me, he will try.

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: The calendar starts ticking. Rent, rivals and salaries are real from today.

captions.speaker: mira
captions.text: Careful with the old sign. It's older than your soldering iron.

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: PHONE REPAIR comes down. {company} goes up.

captions.speaker: felix
captions.text: Same garage, bigger plans. I'll be in the car. Crying a little.

captions.speaker: mira
captions.text: Keep the counter, though. Old customers will still bring you cracked screens.

captions.speaker: radio
captions.text: Night Shift FM: a brand-new phone company on our street. Two a.m. never looked so bright.

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: The story is over. The garage is yours. Now build something huge.

tips: The current objective glows softly. When in doubt, follow the glow.
Left mouse grabs things, right mouse turns them. Yes, you can throw them. Not customers' phones, please.
F turns on the flashlight. The garage has dark corners on purpose.
E works on almost everything: doors, the counter, the bench, the PC, the whiteboard and the van.
Tab opens the quick menu with all the company screens.
T opens the chat. Every line you type is spoken out loud by your character.
Invite friends with the room code from the top bar. A company can have up to four founders.
Playing together? One of you takes orders at the counter, another repairs. Teamwork beats heroics.
A neat repair pays more: the mini-game score decides how much of the price the customer pays.
Out of screens or batteries? Call the supplier on the garage phone and buy parts in Purchasing.
Crates reach the shops only after they're shipped. Carry them to the van for +5% units.
Crates left in the garage ship by themselves after a week, but without the careful-handling bonus.
Challenges at the PC, the whiteboard and the workbench speed things up. Each one has a cooldown.
The Design Studio shows the critics' forecast after every choice. Check it before you publish.
Supplier contracts can be up to 10% cheaper than buying at the spot price.
In a co-founder company, big spends need every founder's approval.
Bugs found during development can be fixed with research points, or by a Bug Fixer over time.
Hire people at the job board. Happy staff work better; underpaid staff work… creatively.
The workbench is only the beginning: the second floor has room for real production lines.
Rivals launch phones too. Look at their prices before you set yours.
Story mode: the company clock starts in chapter 4. Until then, take all the time you need.
After the story, repair orders still come in. Small side money until the company outgrows the garage.
Fact: 90% of repair is unscrewing things. The other 10% is looking for the screw you dropped.
If a customer says "I didn't do anything, it just broke", it fell into water.
A good phone is one you'd buy yourself. A great one is one your grandma can use.
Coffee doesn't speed up the game clock. It just feels like it does.
The bell on the counter has never been repaired. It doesn't need repairs. It's perfect.
